prd_sections.title: Overview
prd_sections.summary: Foundational identity namespace for actors, auth users, sessions, and actor capability context.

prd_sections.title: Two-Layer Identity Model
prd_sections.summary: Distinguishes immutable agent templates from runtime actor instances with context.

prd_sections.title: Table Details
prd_sections.summary: Defines identity and memory-linked tables including lupo_auth_users, lupo_actors, lupo_sessions, and lupo_memory_nodes.

prd_sections.title: Cross-Namespace Dependencies
prd_sections.summary: Declares actor and agent attribution dependencies into channels, agents, content, truth, and governance namespaces.

prd_sections.title: Memory Doctrine Addendum
prd_sections.summary: Defines four edge dimensions and needs_review review_reason requirements for memory graph integrity.

prd_rules.summary: No foreign keys, triggers, or stored procedures; timestamps are BIGINT UTC; IDs are generated in application logic.
Agents are immutable templates while actors are runtime contextual entities; do not conflate identity layers.
Expired sessions are soft-deleted by setting is_deleted, deleted_ymdhis, and updated_ymdhis.
Every memory edge requires type, context, status, and direction dimensions.
When edge_status is needs_review, review_reason must be populated.

definitions.meaning: Immutable filesystem template under agents keyed by agent metadata.
Runtime operational identity with context, attribution, and mutable state.
First-class memory entity represented in lupo_memory_nodes.
Epistemic state for conflicting/incomplete relationships that require agent or human review.
Retention-safe deletion pattern using is_deleted and deleted_ymdhis fields.
